tiers.description: No agent action. A human actor performs the work end-to-end. KYE Protocol is not in the path; downstream compliance applies as it would for any non-AI workflow.
example_use_cases: An adviser drafts a will by hand with no AI tooling.
A claims handler resolves a case in the legacy case-management system without agent assistance.

tiers.description: The agent suggests, drafts, or summarises; a human reviews and decides. The human owns the decision and the audit record. KYE Protocol is optional and recommended only when the assistance materially shapes the decision.
example_use_cases: An adviser uses an AI assistant to draft clause-suggestions which the adviser reviews before signing.
A risk analyst uses an LLM to summarise a 30-page exposure report before manually scoring it.

tiers.description: The agent acts inside a pre-declared Purpose Permission grant for a bounded class of actions. Every action passes through admissibility, emits an evidence pack, and is replayable. A human approver remains on-call for critical-point reviews. KYE Protocol is required.
example_use_cases: An estate-planning agent assembles a draft will and lifts each clause-novelty above the firm's threshold for adviser approval.
A payment-orchestration agent reconciles invoices within a single counterparty scope; transfers above a threshold escalate to two-person review.

tiers.description: The agent acts under bundled authority — a compiled grant + federation chain — and reports finality. Every action is admissibility-gated, evidenced, replayable, and recorded against the authority finality register. A supervisor is on the loop only for declared exceptions. Every KAC-1..KAC-12 is operating.
example_use_cases: A cross-organisation procurement agent issues purchase orders within a federated authority bundle, reporting authority finality on each issuance.
A regulated-data steward agent runs a bounded DSAR pipeline end-to-end, with replay-proof evidence on every read and every release.
